title: Negative translation of classical propositional proofs

based_on.title: Classical and constructive logic (revised November 2, 2001)
based_on.pages: Section 7 pp. 18–19, recursive translation, Theorem 7.1 including translated hypotheses.

based_on.title: Intuitionistic Logic (ILLC report PP-2006-25; ESSLLI 2005 lectures)
based_on.pages: Section 3.5 printed pp. 22–23, Definition 29, Theorem 30 and proof including translated hypotheses.

summary: Interpret classical propositional proofs intuitionistically by translating their formulas, with stability, exact consequence and substitution laws.
abstract: Excluded middle has a classical proof, while its double-negated form already has an intuitionistic proof. A negative translation extends this observation to every classical propositional proof by changing its formulas and open assumptions together. The translated conclusion has a special stability property that allows its double negation to be removed, so even a classical contradiction step can be replaced by intuitionistic rules. We prove this translation directly on proof trees and show that the translated intuitionistic consequences are exactly the original classical consequences. Translation keeps Boolean truth and atom names unchanged, while its interaction with formula substitution requires intuitionistic equivalence rather than literal equality.
